verified_behaviors: Qualified JuiceFS internal control inode exists under the backing Candidate; both control names are rejected at two gateway depths. Special inode ranges and foreign owners are rejected, while tenant .config/settings works.
All supported FUSE modifying requests serialize through a trusted operation lock and synchronize backing writes before acknowledgement; reads use direct IO.

Seal closes admission before joining an already admitted mutation. A real SIGSTOP of the exact native JuiceFS client prevents a positive drain receipt while a write is active; SIGCONT permits it to finish.
UID/GID 1000 workload with no supplementary groups creates, writes, synchronizes, renames, removes names and changes timestamps through the actual mount. Shared shared writable mmap is rejected.
After seal, old linked and unlinked descriptors cannot write. Truncate, create, mkdir, rename, unlink, rmdir, chmod and utime fail with EROFS. Reads return the original durable content.
An independent read-only JuiceFS client with disabled data cache reads seven expected bytes from the same qualified volume after sealing.

Real synchronization failure prevents a positive receipt permanently. Unit tests also reject path escapes, hardlink aliases, privileged modes and foreign UIDs, and prove pinned inode behavior across path replacement.
Mount receipt is an opaque Rust handle; audit JSON and diagnostic status cannot recreate successful drain or database writer authority.
